chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn 'Abdus, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Layth al-Muradi, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man's istinja' using a bone, dung, or a stick. He said: "As for the bone and dung, they are the food of the jinn, and that is among the things they stipulated to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله." Then he said: "It is not proper with anything of that."

key_terms.اشْتَرَطُوا: they stipulated or set as a condition
key_terms.الرَّوْثُ: dung, identified here as food for the jinn
key_terms.الْجِنِّ: the jinn, for whom bone and dung are described as food
key_terms.الْعَظْمُ: bone, mentioned here as an unsuitable material for istinja'
key_terms.لَا يَصْلُحُ: it is not proper or suitable

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform istinja' with bone, dung, or wood in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning istinja' and states that using bone and dung is not proper. It also explains that bone and dung are food for the jinn and mentions this as something they stipulated to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.
